A coordinate-labelled inclusion diamond materially clarifies how the same nonzero overlap sits in both summands while their sum fills the ambient space. A literal real-plane picture would be misleading over arbitrary fields; this set-inclusion schematic works over every field.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Top label U+W=F^3; nonzero e_1 in bottom node.

Independent coordinate-basis check: U has basis (1,0,0),(0,1,0); W has basis (0,1,0),(0,0,1); I has basis (0,1,0); F^3 has the three coordinate vectors. Comparing coordinates proves independence and spanning over every field, hence dimensions 2,2,1,3. These dimension claims are not added to this early-library item.

Exhaustive local enumeration over F_2,F_3,F_5 produced (|U|,|W|,|I|,|U+W|)=(4,4,2,8),(9,9,3,27),(25,25,5,125), with nonzero e_1 in I in each case. Generic coordinate reasoning above supplies the arbitrary-field justification.
